record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: Does every oriented graph D have a vertex v whose second out-neighborhood has cardinality at least its in-neighborhood, that is, |N++(v)| >= |N-(v)|?

evidence.quote: Sullivan [64] posed the following variation of Seymour’s Conjecture.
Conjecture 7.2 Every oriented graph D has a vertex v whose second out-neighborhood N ++(v) is not smaller than its in-neighborhood N −(v).

artifact.status_search_result: Sullivan's second neighborhood conjecture (a variant of Seymour's conjecture) remains open in general. It has been verified for several special classes — including quasi-transitive oriented graphs, orientations of planar graphs, and orientations of triangle-free graphs — and partial progress (e.g., counts of "Sullivan-1" vertices) has appeared as recently as 2024–2025, but no proof or counterexample for arbitrary oriented graphs is known.

status_evidence.title: On Seymour's and Sullivan's Second Neighbourhood Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Studies both Seymour's and Sullivan's conjectures, providing sufficient conditions and verifying special cases; treats them as open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Sullivan's conjecture treated as an unresolved problem with partial results.
